findings.detail: With core.symlinks=true, a present sparse-excluded symlink can become a regular file without invalidating review. Capture docs/link with dirty link text 'changed-target', then replace it with a regular file containing exactly those bytes. The normalized passes omit updates outside the sparse cone, retaining mode 120000. This branch accepts the regular file and hashes its bytes while still recording mode 120000. Both content trees, semantic index and already-dirty bucket membership can therefore remain identical, leaving snapshot unchanged despite the type change. Determine the current disk kind for present sparse paths; preserve the regular link-text exception specifically for core.symlinks=false. Both canonical helper copies are affected.
findings.evidence: Static trace: working_tree_digest at lines 266-269 runs git add without --sparse; the installed git-add documentation states that these operations do not update entries outside the sparse cone. raw_tree_digest takes mode from that index at line 298, accepts a regular file in the 120000 branch at lines 321-324, and writes the unchanged mode at line 328. The digest at lines 633-639 contains those trees and path/bucket membership, with no independent disk-kind field. A dirty symlink and its same-text regular replacement consequently have identical captured values. The new consistency guard permits this retained normalized tree when raw_tree differs from HEAD. Existing sparse coverage tests the regular link-text case only after disabling core.symlinks.
findings.title: Sibling input forms: sparse symlink replacements retain the indexed file type
